articles.description: Thousands of Israelis have taken to the streets of Tel Aviv to protest against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, just days before Israel’s October 27, 2026, general election. The protesters are demanding an independent state commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks. Families of victims and former hostages have called for accountability, while opposition leaders have joined the demonstrations. Netanyahu has resisted calls for an independent inquiry, proposing a different investigative mechanism. Opposition parties have pledged to establish a state commission of inquiry if they take power. With public anger, political divisions and uncertainty over the formation of a governing majority, the election is being closely watched as a major test for Netanyahu’s leadership. articles.title: ‘Netanyahu Must Go’: 100,000+ Israelis Protest In Tel Aviv; Heat On PM Bibi Before Election | Watch
articles.description: Thousands of Israelis took to the streets of Tel Aviv on October 24 to protest against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his government, just days before Israel’s October 27 election. Demonstrators gathered at Hostages Square, demanding accountability for the security failures that preceded the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack, which killed around 1,200 people and triggered the war in Gaza. Organised by the October Council, the protest brought together critics of Netanyahu’s leadership, including families of hostages, activists and former military officials. Demonstrators called for an independent inquiry into the October 7 attack and voiced concerns over corruption, the state of Israeli democracy and the government’s handling of the conflict. Some protesters expressed hope that the election could bring political change, while others warned of deeper public frustration if Netanyahu remains in power.

articles.title: Iran’s Ghalibaf to Skip BRICS Forum in Delhi, Cites ‘Unforeseen Circumstances’ | News18
articles.description: Iran’s parliamentary speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, will not attend the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum in New Delhi, with the Iranian embassy citing “unforeseen circumstances” for his absence. In a statement issued on Saturday, the embassy confirmed that Ghalibaf, speaker of Iran’s Islamic Consultative Assembly, would be unable to participate in the meeting of parliamentary speakers from BRICS member countries. An Iranian parliamentary delegation will attend the forum in his place. Despite the speaker’s absence, Tehran has reiterated its commitment to active participation in BRICS summits and meetings. The embassy said the Iranian delegation would continue dialogue and consultations with representatives of other member countries, with a focus on strengthening bilateral and multilateral cooperation, particularly in parliamentary relations.
